title: Negative-capacitance HZO layer fused onto ZrO2 storage capacitor
idea: Combine a thin ferroelectric HZO film, biased in its non-switching negative-capacitance regime, in series with the paraelectric ZrO2/Al2O3 cell dielectric so the ferroelectric's negative dQ/dV cancels part of the dielectric's inverse capacitance. Thickness-match the layers so the stack stays hysteresis-free while effective k reaches ~70-100 in the same 60:1 pillar.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): hits the k~70 target without going to AR 115; 1.5-2x Cs or 30-40% shorter pillars with fewer etch/deposition steps.

title: Coaxial pillar: storage capacitor core inside vertical transistor shell
idea: Fuse access transistor and capacitor into one vertical pillar: a grounded TiN core plate, a high-k sleeve, and a doped-oxide storage-node shell form the capacitor, and the same shell continues upward as a short vertical channel gated by a wordline ring at the pillar top. The capacitor uses the pillar volume and the transistor uses the pillar skin, so one pillar is one 4F2 cell with no landing pad.
why: Density 6F2 to 4F2 (+33% bits/area) and removes the storage-node contact and landing-pad litho layers; attacks facts 2 and 4.

title: Pseudocapacitive redox storage node borrowed from supercapacitors
idea: Coat the storage-node electrode with 1-2 nm of hydrous MnO2 (or another fast surface-redox oxide) behind a thin blocking oxide, so surface faradaic reactions store charge on top of the dielectric's electrostatic charge, as in supercapacitor electrodes (hundreds of uF/cm2). The cell becomes a nano-supercapacitor with 10-50x the areal charge of a plain MIM stack.
why: Fact 1: a planar or AR<10 capacitor could reach 5 fF, collapsing the high-AR etch and multi-step ALD module (cost per bit, capital); the open question is whether redox kinetics keep up at ns timescales.

title: Separate capacitor wafer hybrid-bonded to transistor wafer at cell pitch
idea: Combine deep-trench decoupling-capacitor manufacturing (mature, DUV-only) with sub-500 nm pitch wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding: one wafer carries only dense trench capacitors, the other carries access transistors and periphery, and each cell's storage node is joined by a Cu-Cu pad. Each wafer is optimized and yield-screened separately, and the capacitor wafer can come from a low-capital U.S. MEMS or passive-component fab.
why: Capital intensity and U.S. manufacturability (facts 4, 7): no EUV in the capacitor flow and parallel fabs; claimed 20-30% wafer cost cut; bond pitch and overlay are the risks.

title: Vertical CCD charge-packet strings using 3D NAND tier stacks
idea: Fuse 1970s CCD memory with 3D NAND's stacked-gate vertical channel: 128 wordline tiers around a vertical poly-Si or IGZO channel are clocked in three phases to shift charge packets up and down, so bits live as packets in potential wells with no per-bit capacitor or lateral transistor. A sense amp at the string top reads packets as they arrive: serial within a string, massively parallel across millions of strings.
why: Fact 2: a 3D storage element with no capacitor and no lateral transistor, reusing NAND tooling; 5-10x bits per mm2 at block-sequential latency of a few hundred ns.

title: Single-electron transistor sensing attofarad storage nodes
idea: Combine a room-temperature silicon single-electron transistor (sub-3 nm island) as the in-cell sense element with a 10-50 aF storage node, so a few hundred electrons, not ~30,000, encode a bit. The SET's Coulomb oscillations turn each few-electron change into a large current change, read through a gain path that never discharges the node.
why: Facts 1 and 10: the capacitor shrinks ~100x (no high-AR pillars) and storage swings can drop to ~0.3 V; write energy falls ~10x.

title: Threshold-switch selector stacked on capacitor for cross-point 3D DRAM
idea: Fuse the ovonic threshold switch selector from 3D XPoint with a MIM capacitor into a two-terminal 1S1C stack at each wordline/bitline crossing, built in 8-16 decks with no transistor. Half-select bias stays below the OTS threshold to isolate the node; a full-select pulse snaps the OTS on to charge or sense it.
why: Facts 2 and 4: 4F2 per deck with no front-end transistor; 8 decks ~5x density per wafer; requires OTS sub-threshold leakage below ~1 fA.

title: Split-pillar complementary capacitor in one etched hole
idea: Etch a single capacitor hole, then split its bottom electrode lengthwise into two half-shells separated by a dielectric fin, so one hole holds a true and a complement storage node sharing one plate. Complementary charges give a differential 2x signal that cancels plate and coupling noise.
why: Fact 1: 2x sense margin per hole lets each half carry ~40% less charge (shorter pillar); differential sensing also improves row-hammer tolerance (fact 9).

title: Porphyrin redox monolayer giving multi-level charge per node
idea: Graft a monolayer of porphyrin or ferrocene molecules with 2-3 discrete oxidation states onto the storage-node electrode, combining molecular electronics with the DRAM capacitor so charge sits in molecular redox states at fixed potentials. Discrete states give quantized charge levels (2 bits/cell), and electrons must cross a molecular tether barrier to escape, stretching retention from 64 ms toward minutes.
why: Facts 1 and 3: 2 bits/cell plus up to ~1000x longer retention cuts refresh power; molecule stability over 1e15 cycles is the risk.

title: Cryogenic quantum-paraelectric SrTiO3 capacitor at 77 K
idea: Combine liquid-nitrogen-cooled memory pools with SrTiO3 or KTaO3, quantum paraelectrics whose permittivity climbs from ~300 at room temperature to over 1000 near 77 K. A 5 nm STO film in a planar or AR-10 capacitor then delivers 5 fF without high-AR pillars.
why: Fact 1 and capital: k rises 15-50x over ZrO2, so the capacitor module drops from 60:1 etch to near-planar (~50% lower capacitor-module capex); thin-film k is below bulk, which is the risk.

title: WDM optical readout of quantum-dot charge storage cells
idea: Fuse silicon-photonic wavelength multiplexing with charge storage: each cell is a quantum dot coupled to a micro-ring whose resonance shifts through the quantum-confined Stark effect when the dot holds charge. One waveguide carrying 64 wavelengths reads 64 cells at once, non-destructively, with no bitline or sense amp.
why: Facts 5, 7, 8: no destructive read or page overfetch, data leaves the array as light at ~0.1-0.5 pJ/bit, and the sense-amp periphery shrinks.

title: Tunnel-FET gain cell with steep-slope read amplification
idea: Combine a band-to-band tunneling FET (sub-30 mV/decade) as the read device with a small storage node in a 2T gain cell, so every 10 mV of stored voltage moves read current by about an order of magnitude. Storage nodes can be 0.5 fF or less at a 0.4 V swing, and reading never disturbs the node.
why: Facts 1, 8, 10: ~10x smaller Cs, 0.4 V operation for ~6x lower CV2 energy, and non-destructive read.

title: Four-level DRAM cell using flash-style program-and-verify
idea: Combine NAND flash's incremental-step program-and-verify loop with DRAM charge storage: the write driver applies short pulses and senses the node between pulses until it lands in one of four charge windows, storing 2 bits per cell. A gain read device and a reference ladder resolve the levels, and refresh re-centers each level.
why: Density and cost per bit (fact 4): 2x bits/cell without a node shrink, worth several nodes of 10-20% scaling; write latency roughly doubles.

title: Gen-10.5 display-glass fabs building IGZO capacitor memory panels
idea: Combine display-panel manufacturing (Gen-10.5 glass, 2-3 um lines, IGZO backplanes already in volume) with 1T1C memory: pattern memory arrays across square meters of glass at roughly a cent per cm2, then cut them into large capacity-tier panels attached by flex to CXL controllers. It trades density for ~1000x cheaper area and zero EUV.
why: Capital and scarce tools (fact 4): uses idle display capacity outside the EUV supply chain; cost per bit could approach parity for capacity tiers; latency, RC and physical size are the risks.

title: Nanoporous dealloyed metal electrode inside storage capacitor
idea: Borrow dealloyed nanoporous metals from battery and catalyst electrodes: deposit a TiAl alloy in a wider, shallower capacitor hole, selectively etch out the Al to leave a sponge with 10-20 nm pores, then coat ALD dielectric and top electrode throughout. The sponge multiplies internal surface area 3-4x within the same footprint.
why: Fact 1: 3-4x area allows AR ~20:1 instead of 60-75:1 at the same Cs, cutting deep-etch time and tool count.

title: Anodic rutile TiO2 dielectric grown like electrolytic capacitors
idea: Combine electrolytic-capacitor anodization with DRAM: line the capacitor hole with Ti and anodize it in a non-aqueous electrolyte, growing a conformal, self-limiting oxide whose thickness is set by voltage, on a rutile SnO2 template so it crystallizes as rutile TiO2 (k~80-100). Electrochemistry coats any aspect ratio without ALD, and weak spots self-heal because current crowds there and grows more oxide.
why: Fact 1 and capital: k~80 meets the k~70 target; wet electrochemical cells replace several ALD chambers; self-healing trims the leakage tail (fact 3).

title: Si/SiGe superlattice selectively oxidized into 100-plate stacked capacitor
idea: Combine GAA nanosheet epitaxy with selective conversion: grow 100 alternating Si/SiGe layers, cut a slit, replace the SiGe with high-k through Ge-selective etch and ALD refill, and silicide alternate Si sheets contacted from two opposite staircases to form an interdigitated stack. Horizontal plates become stacked storage capacitors for 3D DRAM tiers with no vertical high-AR hole.
why: Facts 1 and 2: capacitance grows with tier count instead of AR, and one epi stack serves both transistor and capacitor tiers, aiming at the 26+ tier break-even.

title: NEMS parametron storing bits as oscillation phase
idea: Revive Goto's 1950s parametron with GHz nanomechanical resonators: each cell is an AlN or SiN nanobeam pumped at twice its resonance, so it oscillates in one of two phases (0 or pi) that encode the bit. A shared pump line drives thousands of resonators, and phase is read by capacitive pickoff against a reference without destroying it.
why: Facts 3, 8, 9: no charge leakage tail, non-destructive read, no row hammer; high-Q (>1e4) resonators keep shared pump power low; density is the risk.

title: Logic-fab BEOL finger capacitors as DRAM storage nodes
idea: Combine the metal-oxide-metal finger capacitors that every logic back-end already offers with BEOL oxide-semiconductor access transistors, so a standard logic interconnect stack (interdigitated M3-M8 lines) becomes the storage capacitor field. No special capacitor module, high-AR etch or memory fab is needed: any U.S. logic fab can print DRAM-class memory above its own logic.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital: uses existing domestic back-end tooling with zero new capex; density is ~1/3 of commodity DRAM but the memory sits on-die (fact 5).

title: Block-copolymer self-assembly patterning hexagonal capacitor arrays
idea: Combine directed self-assembly of PS-b-PMMA cylinders, which form hexagonal close-packed arrays at 20-28 nm pitch, with the DRAM capacitor array, which is already hexagonal: a coarse DUV prepattern guides the cylinders, which are transferred into a hard mask to define capacitor holes. Spin-on chemistry replaces one or two EUV or quad-patterning layers.
why: Fact 4: removes EUV from the capacitor level; ~5-8% wafer cost reduction and less dependence on the single EUV supplier.

title: MOS varactor storage node with self-amplifying C-V nonlinearity
idea: Combine an RF varactor with the storage capacitor: build the node as an accumulation-mode MOS capacitor whose capacitance is high when charged to '1' and drops ~3x near '0', so the stored charge difference exceeds that of a linear capacitor of the same average size. The C-V nonlinearity acts as built-in gain at charge-share time.
why: Fact 1: ~1.5-2x sense signal per unit area, which relaxes AR or allows a lower array voltage (fact 10).

title: Revive deep-trench SOI eDRAM as U.S.-made memory chiplets
idea: Combine the deep-trench SOI eDRAM process once used in IBM POWER and z processors with chiplet and hybrid-bond stacking: a U.S. fab builds dense eDRAM-only chiplets on existing 14-22 nm SOI lines and stacks them into HBM-like cubes. Trench capacitors (~20-40 fF) are proven, and the lines are already depreciated.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital: domestic, EUV-free supply; large trench Cs also eases refresh; density ~1/4 of commodity DRAM but sovereign.

title: High-entropy fluorite oxide dielectric suppressing crystallization leakage paths
idea: Combine the high-entropy-alloy concept with the storage dielectric: an ALD supercycle mixes five cations (Hf, Zr, Ti, Ce, Sn) into one oxide so configurational entropy stabilizes a single fine-grained high-k phase and blocks the grain-boundary leakage paths that cripple pure TiO2 or ZrO2 at k>50. Target: k~50-60 with ZrO2-class leakage.
why: Facts 1 and 3: ~1.5x Cs at equal leakage and a tighter leakage tail; avoids scarce Ta, Nb and Ru.

title: Bistable buckled nanobeam storing bits as mechanical position
idea: Combine a pre-compressed (buckled) SiC nanobeam, which has two stable shapes, with a capacitive-gap read: an electrostatic pulse snaps the beam up or down, and the beam's position sets the capacitance to a sense electrode. Mechanical bistability holds the bit with zero hold current and no refresh; nanoscale beams switch in ~10 ns.
why: Facts 3 and 9: refresh (16-33% of idle power) and row hammer both disappear because there is no charge to leak or disturb; SiC MEMS show >1e12-cycle fatigue life.

title: NEMS air-gap relay as zero-leakage access switch for capacitor
idea: Replace the access transistor with a vertical nanoelectromechanical relay whose off state is a 5 nm vacuum gap: no channel and no junction, so off-current is essentially zero and the capacitor keeps its charge for days, limited only by dielectric leakage. Carbon or TiN contacts sit under a hermetic BEOL cap, and a negative-stiffness spring lets the relay close in a few ns below 1 V.
why: Fact 3: the 13 fA leakage tail vanishes, so refresh drops from ~46 fJ/bit to zero; low pull-in voltage also removes the 3 V wordline (fact 10).

title: Vacuum nanochannel field-emission valve as cell access device
idea: Fuse vacuum-tube electronics with the DRAM cell: each storage node reaches the bitline through a sealed 10-20 nm vacuum gap between a sharp emitter tip and a collector, gated by a ring electrode. Below the field-emission threshold no carrier exists in the gap, so the node cannot leak; raising the gate field emits electrons for ns-speed write and read.
why: Fact 3: refresh eliminated; the vacuum gap is temperature-insensitive, so hot (125 C) operation carries no retention penalty, and it is radiation hard.

title: Ultra-wide-bandgap Ga2O3 or diamond access transistor locks charge
idea: Combine power-electronics materials with the DRAM cell: a thin-film beta-Ga2O3 (4.8 eV) or hydrogen-terminated diamond access transistor built in BEOL has thermal-generation and band-to-band leakage far below 1e-21 A, so a 1-5 fF node keeps its charge for years. Bits are written like DRAM and held like flash, with unlimited endurance because nothing tunnels through an oxide.
why: Fact 3: refresh power goes to zero and 10-20% bandwidth returns; goes past IGZO's ~3.2 eV gap that prior work studied.

title: BEOL complementary oxide latch: n-IGZO plus p-SnO cross-coupled
idea: Combine n-type IGZO with p-type SnO or Cu2O thin-film transistors into a cross-coupled CMOS latch built in the back-end and stacked 4-8 tiers over logic. Like SRAM it holds state statically with no refresh, but oxide off-currents (~1e-19 A) make standby power ~1000x lower than silicon SRAM.
why: Facts 3 and 2: refresh-free, monolithic 3D tiers over logic; lower density per tier than DRAM but multiplied by tier count; p-type oxide mobility is the risk.

title: Charge-active, polarization-parked hybrid capacitor rows
idea: Combine a DRAM capacitor and a FeRAM capacitor in one ZrO2/HZO bilayer: rows in active use run as fast volatile charge cells, and when a row sits idle past ~10 ms the controller issues one plate pulse that copies its charge state into the ferroelectric polarization and powers the row down. Idle rows cost zero refresh, and the first access restores them to charge mode.
why: Fact 3: refresh energy on idle data (most of capacity) goes to zero with no change to active performance; ferroelectric wear is spent only per park (~1e6 parks/year).

title: Work-function-imprinted antiferroelectric ZrO2 nonvolatile cell
idea: Combine antiferroelectric ZrO2's double hysteresis (fatigue-resistant, 1e11+ cycles) with asymmetric electrodes, a TiN bottom and a high-work-function MoO3-capped top, whose built-in field shifts one AFE loop to straddle 0 V. The film then holds two remanent states at zero bias like a ferroelectric but switches through the gentler field-induced AFE transition.
why: Zero refresh with endurance beyond HZO FeRAM; a nonvolatile 1T1C at DRAM-like ~1 V using no tungsten, ruthenium or platinum.

title: Strain-coupled piezo layer flipping a magnetostrictive nanomagnet
idea: Combine a thin AlScN piezoelectric pad with an elliptical magnetostrictive FeGa nanomagnet on top: a voltage pulse strains the magnet and rotates its easy axis by 90 degrees, and a timed pulse pair completes a 180-degree flip. A tunnel junction stacked above reads the state; writing draws almost no current, and the magnet holds the bit indefinitely.
why: Zero refresh, ~1 aJ writes (about 100x below STT-MRAM), effectively unlimited magnetic endurance; AlScN is CMOS-compatible.

title: Conductive ferroelectric domain walls in thin-film lithium niobate
idea: Combine the thin-film lithium niobate photonics platform with domain-wall nanoelectronics: a voltage writes or erases a charged domain wall between two electrodes, and the wall conducts 1e3-1e6x more than the bulk crystal. Read is a small non-destructive current through the wall, and the polarization holds the bit with no refresh.
why: Zero refresh plus non-destructive read (fact 8); LiNbO3 domain walls show >1e10-cycle endurance and fast switching; U.S. TFLN foundries exist.

title: Ferroelectric semiconductor channel: alpha-In2Se3 holds bit in itself
idea: Fuse channel and storage element: alpha-In2Se3 is a 2D semiconductor whose own lattice is ferroelectric, so switching its polarization changes the channel conductance directly. A one-transistor cell with no gate ferroelectric and no capacitor stores the bit in the channel and reads it non-destructively.
why: Zero refresh in a 1T 4F2 cell without the interface-trap fatigue of FeFET gate stacks; indium supply and 2D growth uniformity are risks.

title: Antiferromagnetic Mn3Sn bit written by spin-orbit torque
idea: Combine the noncollinear antiferromagnet Mn3Sn with a BiSb topological-insulator spin-orbit-torque write line and a tunnel-magnetoresistance read: the antiferromagnetic order switches in picoseconds, produces no stray field so cells pack at pitch without crosstalk, and ignores external fields. The order is stable at zero power.
why: Zero refresh, dense packing with no stray-field spacing, ps switching and effectively unlimited endurance; small read signal is the risk; avoids W and Pt write lines.

title: Liquid-nitrogen immersed DRAM racks where retention outlasts data
idea: Combine LN2 immersion cooling (already used for HTS cables and extreme overclocking) with commodity DRAM pools: at 77 K access-transistor leakage falls by many orders of magnitude, stretching retention from 64 ms to hours, so refresh is simply switched off. Cryo also speeds transistors ~20% and cuts wire resistance several-fold.
why: Zero refresh power and 10-20% bandwidth recovered; cooling overhead (~10 W input per W removed at 77 K) must be amortized at disaggregated memory-pool scale.

title: Short-retention cells matched to ephemeral AI tensors
idea: Combine compiler-known tensor lifetimes with deliberately cheap short-retention cells: activations, KV-cache pages and gradients that are overwritten within 50 ms go to a pool whose cells retain only ~100 ms worst case and are never refreshed. A runtime time-to-live tag per page rewrites or evicts data before expiry, so refresh disappears and the capacitor can be ~3x smaller.
why: Zero refresh power for the AI-dominant data class, and a smaller Cs (fact 1) allows lower AR and a cheaper process.

title: Thin-film flux-closure nanorings: magnetic core memory reborn
idea: Combine 1960s ferrite core memory with thin-film lithography: each bit is a 50-100 nm CoFeB ring whose vortex magnetization circulates clockwise or counterclockwise, switched by a current pulse through a central via and read by a TMR sensor at the ring edge. Closed flux means no stray field between neighbours and no refresh.
why: Zero refresh and unlimited endurance (no tunnel barrier in the write path), radiation hard, 6-10F2 cells.

title: Convert U.S. hard-disk read-head fabs to spin-memory element lines
idea: Combine the hard-drive industry's thin-film head wafer fabs in Minnesota, which already deposit and pattern TMR stacks at sub-30 nm, with back-end memory integration: contract them to make refresh-free magnetic storage-element wafers that are bonded onto CMOS periphery made elsewhere. As head volumes decline, the tools and TMR know-how convert to memory.
why: U.S. manufacturability and zero refresh: domestic, depreciated magnetic thin-film capacity instead of a new $15B fab.

title: Ferroelectric tunnel door sealing a capacitor's charge
idea: Combine a ferroelectric tunnel junction with a storage capacitor: the only path into the node is a 2-3 nm ferroelectric barrier whose polarization toggles it between transparent and opaque (tunneling ratio >1e5). The door is switched open for a write and closed to lock the charge, while a separate gain transistor reads the node without opening it.
why: Zero refresh while keeping charge storage (unlimited reads); the ferroelectric switches only on writes; closed-state tunneling must reach sub-aA levels.

title: Spin-crossover molecular dielectric with room-temperature hysteresis
idea: Combine iron(II)-triazole spin-crossover complexes, which switch between low-spin and high-spin states with ~10% volume and permittivity change and show 20-40 K wide hysteresis around room temperature, with a capacitor read: a local heating or field pulse flips the molecular layer, and capacitance reports the state. The bistable spin state holds without power.
why: Zero refresh in a ~5 nm molecular layer that could stack densely; switching speed and cycling endurance are the risks.

title: Sliding-ferroelectric bilayer hBN: fatigue-free interlayer shift bit
idea: Combine 2D-material stacking with ferroelectric memory: in parallel-stacked bilayer hBN, sliding one layer by a fraction of a lattice constant flips an out-of-plane dipole, and an adjacent MoS2 channel senses the dipole as a threshold shift. Because no bonds break and no ions migrate, switching is reported nearly fatigue-free.
why: Zero refresh with endurance approaching unlimited and sub-ns switching; wafer-scale aligned stacking is the risk.

title: Via-programmed ROM for frozen model weights frees DRAM
idea: Combine mask-ROM economics with AI inference: weights frozen for a product's life are encoded in one via layer (1-2F2 per bit, multi-level via resistance for 2 bits) on a die whose other masks are shared, so only the via mask changes per model, written by e-beam or DUV. The weights never need refresh, never wear out, and stop occupying HBM.
why: Weights are a large share of inference memory; moving them to refresh-free ROM at ~1/5 the cost per bit releases that DRAM supply.

title: Light-gated photoconductive switch isolating a dark capacitor
idea: Combine a wide-bandgap GaN thin-film photoconductor as the access switch with a storage capacitor: in the dark the switch is an insulator (~1e-20 A), and a nanosecond pulse from a row waveguide or micro-LED makes it conduct for write and read. With no electrical gate on the access path, the node holds charge for days without refresh.
why: Zero refresh and no 3 V wordline (fact 10), since the wordline is delivered as light; persistent photoconductivity is the risk.

title: Defect charge-state memory in silicon carbide color centers
idea: Combine quantum-sensing color centers with memory: divacancies in 4H-SiC switch between stable charge states when an electrical pulse injects carriers in a p-i-n structure, and the charge state persists for hours to years in the dark. Read is electrical, through the defect ensemble's effect on junction capacitance, at ns speed.
why: Zero refresh, radiation hard, on a material with U.S. production (SiC power wafers); signal per cell and density are speculative.

title: High-temperature superconductor persistent-current loops at 77 K
idea: Combine REBCO high-temperature superconductor films with an LN2 memory rack: each bit is a micro-loop holding a clockwise or counterclockwise persistent supercurrent (one flux quantum), written by a Josephson-junction pulse and read by an adjacent SQUID. Persistent currents do not decay, so refresh energy is zero and write energy is ~1e-19 J.
why: Zero refresh and sub-aJ writes; REBCO junction reproducibility and micron-scale loops limit density.

title: Thermally locked ionic glass gating: ions frozen between writes
idea: Combine electric-double-layer ionic gating with a glass transition: the gate dielectric is an ionic glass whose ions move only above ~120 C, so a nanoscale heater line warms one cell for ~10 ns to drive ions and set the channel charge, and on cooling the ions freeze in place. The channel conductance stores the bit with no hold power.
why: Zero refresh; EDL gating gives ~1e14 cm-2 charge density for a large read signal; thermal write energy and speed are risks.
